subject: Connectivity acceptance corridor and structured-output queries (Concord Health)
messages:
From: Alan Wu <alan.wu@concordhealth.com>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@concordhealth.com>
Date: Sun, 9 May 2027 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Acceptance corridor + structured outputs questions

Hi Jonas,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We want to move the streaming + tool-calling feature into our acceptance corridor next week, but the security and clinical teams have a couple of clarifying asks before we sign off on go-live: 

1) Structured outputs: we need an authoritative JSON schema for the clinical summary event, and a clear change control process if the schema evolves. Will your schema support optional fields and semantic versioning?

2) Streaming + tool-calling: when Redwood calls our Medication Lookup service via the tool interface, what connectivity patterns do you use (outbound from Redwood vs inbound webhook)? We need firewall rules to be provisioned and a short list of endpoints and IP ranges.

3) Acceptance criteria: can you share a short checklist we can include in our runbook? It should include latency targets, successful tool-invocation trace examples, and a failure-mode behavior that our SREs can test.

Attaching our high-level network constraints and an acceptance template.

Goal: have a signed acceptance checklist by Wednesday 5/12 so we can schedule canary on 5/15.

Thanks,
Alan
Principal Product Manager
Concord Health

---
Attachment(s): network_connectivity_requirements.pdf, acceptance-template.xlsx
From: jonas_weber@redwood.ai <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: Alan Wu <alan.wu@concordhealth.com>
Cc: monica_patel@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 9 May 2027 11:24:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Acceptance corridor + structured outputs questions

Alan — good questions, thanks for laying these out. I pulled together a compact acceptance checklist and a first-cut schema (attached). Short answers up front, then attachments + next steps: 

- Schema/versioning: yes, our structured-output schemas use semantic versioning (major.minor.patch). We support optional fields and include a validation mode that returns explicit diff errors when a model emits a field that violates the schema. See concord_structured_output_schema_v1.json attached.

- Tool-calling connectivity: Redwood supports both outbound TLS egress (Redwood -> your service) and inbound webhook for tool invocation. For Concord's setup I'd recommend outbound egress from Redwood to your Medication Lookup API (simpler for auth and tracing). IP ranges and endpoints are in the network_connectivity_requirements.pdf.

- Acceptance checklist highlights (full checklist attached):
  * Latency: 95th percentile end-to-end token-to-tool-response <= 400ms under the canary traffic profile.
  * Correctness: 100 sample prompts with expected structured output must validate against schema v1 with <= 1% regression versus baseline.
  * Tool resiliency: simulated tool timeout (5s) must trigger fallback to cached result or graceful failure message per the checklist.
  * Tracing: every tool invocation must emit a span and a correlation_id that appears in our console.

Next steps I propose: 
1) Concord reviews the attached schema + checklist and marks acceptance fields in the attached acceptance-checklist.xlsx.
2) Ben will share the staging IP ranges and a short runbook for simulated timeouts.
3) Monica will coordinate a 30-min SRE alignment call Monday to finalize firewall rules.

I'll schedule the SRE call and loop in Network. Let me know if you prefer inbound webhook instead and we can flip the plan.

—Jonas
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

---
Attachment(s): concord_structured_output_schema_v1.json, acceptance-checklist.xlsx, network_connectivity_requirements.pdf
